Doppler (optional): not essential; ovarian vascularization can be described and, if color Doppler is available, uterine vascularization as well.

Additional findings to rule out: ovarian cysts, tumors, müllerian malformations, free pelvic fluid, adnexal abnormalities.

Structured ultrasound report template:

Transabdominal pelvic ultrasound
Uterus: anteverted, ___ × ___ × ___ mm (length × AP × transverse), volume ___ mL. Tubular/pear-shaped morphology. Body/cervix ratio ___. Homogeneous myometrium.
Endometrium: not visible / visible, thickness ___ mm.
Right ovary: ___ × ___ × ___ mm, volume ___ mL. ___ follicles present, largest ___ mm, peripheral/diffuse distribution.
Left ovary: ___ × ___ × ___ mm, volume ___ mL. ___ follicles present, largest ___ mm, peripheral/diffuse distribution.
Cul-de-sac: no free fluid.
Conclusion: uterus and ovaries with morphological and biometric features showing no clear ultrasound signs of significant pubertal estrogenization / with ultrasound signs of estrogenization and onset of pubertal development / with pubertal development appropriate for age. guias.html:
Basal 17-OHP (points to adrenal origin): <1.0ng/mL rules out a major 21-hydroxylase deficiency. 1.0-2.0ng/mL gray zone — stimulation test needed. >2.0ng/mL high suspicion of non-classic congenital adrenal hyperplasia (NC-CAH). >10-20ng/mL virtually unequivocal diagnosis of CAH, or suspicion of an adrenal neoplasm (add adrenal ultrasound/CT/MRI).

ACTH stimulation test (250µg IV/IM, 17-OHP at 60 min): post-stimulation >10ng/mL (>1000ng/dL) is the gold standard confirming NC-CAH from 21-hydroxylase deficiency.

CPP — axis suppression with depot GnRH agonists: Leuprolide 3.75-7.5mg IM/SC every 28 days (monthly) or 11.25mg every 84 days (quarterly). Triptorelin 3.75mg IM every 28 days or 11.25mg every 12 weeks. Goal: growth velocity <4-5cm/year, stabilizing Tanner stage and preserving adult height. Discontinuation: once bone age reaches 11.0-11.5 years.

NC-CAH — adrenal suppression: hydrocortisone 8-12mg/m²/day in 2-3 oral doses, with the larger dose at night (suppresses the morning ACTH peak). Indicated for symptomatic accelerated adrenarche, bone age advanced >1.5-2 years, virilization, or compromised predicted height. Follow-up: growth velocity, annual bone age, and periodic 17-OHP/androstenedione/DHEA-S — avoid iatrogenic hypercortisolism.

guias.html:

Class II (unicornuate): failure of one duct. Risk of ectopic pregnancy in the rudimentary horn + preterm birth.

guias.titulo: Tubal patency — HyFoSy, HSG and hysteroscopy
guias.fuente: Piccioni et al. (2017), J Clin Ultrasound · RBMO meta-analysis (2024) · HyFoSy vs. HSG diagnostic agreement study (2025)
guias.html:
HyFoSy (echogenic foam instillation under transvaginal ultrasound, no radiation or iodinated contrast) and HSG show comparable sensitivity/specificity for tubal patency (2024 meta-analysis, 2025 agreement study) — HyFoSy with better tolerability (less pain) and no radiation exposure.

Foam vs. saline (Piccioni 2017): saline medium (classic sonohysterography/SIS) disperses quickly and is limited for assessing the tubal course; foam, more viscous and echogenic, allows visualization of tubal passage and peritoneal spill — this is why it replaced saline when the goal is tubal assessment, while saline remains preferable when the goal is only the endometrial cavity (polyps, submucosal fibroids).

Hysteroscopy does not assess tubal patency (uterine cavity only) — reserved for confirming/treating already-suspected intracavitary findings, not as a first-line tubal-factor study.

Algorithm: HyFoSy = first line (tubal screening + cavity, no radiation) · HSG = valid alternative depending on resources · laparoscopy with chromopertubation = reserved for suspected associated pelvic pathology or an inconclusive result.

guias.fuente: ESHRE Female Infertility Guideline (2023) · Prospective case-control study, Frontiers in Endocrinology (2025)
guias.html:
Unexplained infertility: a complete work-up with normal female and male factors (ovulation, ovarian reserve, tubal patency, uterine cavity, semen analysis) with no identifiable cause, after ≥12 months of trying (or 6 months if ≥35 years).

Stress and unexplained infertility: recent evidence shows an association (not proven causation) between psychological distress measured by validated scales and unexplained infertility — but not with single-time endocrine stress markers (e.g., isolated cortisol), suggesting a phenomenon more complex than a simply hyperactivated HPA axis measurable in one sample.

Clinical implication: psychological support can be offered as an adjunct (well-being/treatment adherence), but it does not replace or delay the standard diagnostic-therapeutic algorithm (ovulation induction, IUI, IVF as appropriate).

guias.titulo: Ovulation induction — Therapeutic choice: Letrozole vs. Clomiphene vs. Gonadotropins
guias.fuente: ASRM Practice Committee (2020), Fertil Steril 113(2):274-282 · Teede et al., Int'l PCOS Guideline (2023), Fertil Steril 120(4):767-793 · ESHRE Female Infertility Guideline (2023), Hum Reprod Open 2023(3):hoad034 · MSPyBS Paraguay (2025), Res. S.G. Nº 050/2025
guias.html:
Letrozole (aromatase inhibitor) — first-line in PCOS/WHO Type II anovulation, especially with overweight/obesity (BMI≥25-30). Higher cumulative ovulation, clinical pregnancy and live-birth rates than clomiphene (PPCOS II trial). Does not block endometrial or cervical estrogen receptors (preserves endometrial thickness and cervical mucus quality). Short half-life (~48h): favors monofollicular development, lower multiple-pregnancy rate.

Clomiphene citrate (SERM): first-line alternative when letrozole is unavailable/not tolerated, or in unexplained infertility (timed intercourse/IUI). Drawback: prolonged peripheral antiestrogenic effect (half-life >2 weeks) — refractory thin endometrium (<7mm) and hostile mucus; higher multifollicular/multiple-pregnancy rate (5-10%, mostly twins) than letrozole.

Exogenous gonadotropins (recombinant FSH / hMG): failure or resistance to oral agents (after 3-6 ovulatory cycles without conception); or Hypogonadotropic Hypogonadism (WHO Type I — hypothalamic-pituitary axis not intact, clomiphene/letrozole do NOT work, requires hMG or FSH+hCG/LH microdose); or as an adjunct in low-complexity/IUI cycles.

guias.titulo: Ovulation induction — Dosing regimens and stimulation protocols
guias.fuente: ASRM Practice Committee (2020), Fertil Steril 113(2):274-282 · ESHRE Female Infertility Guideline (2023), Hum Reprod Open 2023(3):hoad034 · MSPyBS Paraguay (2025), Res. S.G. Nº 050/2025
guias.html:
Letrozole: 2.5mg/day PO x5 days, starting cycle day 2-5. If no ovulation, escalate to 5.0mg/day the next cycle; maximum dose 7.5mg/day x5 days.

Clomiphene citrate: 50mg/day PO x5 days, day 2-5. If no response, increase to 100mg/day; usual maximum 150mg/day x5 days (higher doses do not improve pregnancy rates and worsen the endometrial antiestrogenic effect). Limit: 6 ovulatory cycles.

Gonadotropins — "Low-Dose Step-Up" protocol: strict goal of monofollicular development and OHSS prevention. Starting dose 37.5-50-75 IU/day SC/IM from cycle day 2-3, holding the fixed dose for 7-14 days. If after 14 days there is no follicular selection (no follicle ≥10mm), increase 50% weekly (e.g. 37.5→75 IU/day) until a response is seen, then maintain that dose through the trigger.

guias.titulo: Ovulation induction — Baseline and serial ultrasound monitoring
guias.fuente: ASRM Practice Committee (2020), Fertil Steril 113(2):274-282 · ESHRE Female Infertility Guideline (2023), Hum Reprod Open 2023(3):hoad034
guias.html:
Baseline transvaginal ultrasound + Antral Follicle Count (AFC), cycle days 2-4 — mandatory before starting any inducing agent: thin, shed endometrium (<5mm); rule out functional cysts/persistent follicles from the previous cycle (start if no follicles/cysts >10mm; postpone/cancel if a residual cyst or growing follicle ≥10-15mm is found, usually with baseline E2 >50-60pg/mL).

AFC (bilateral 2-9mm follicles): <5-7 suggests low ovarian reserve · 8-15 normal reserve · ≥20 (or ovarian volume ≥10mL) polycystic ovarian morphology — maximum alert for hyperresponse and OHSS risk.

Serial follow-up: first post-stimulation scan on cycle day 8-10, then every 48-72h depending on follicular growth rate (expected physiologic growth 1.5-2mm/day). Record the mean diameter in 2 perpendicular planes per ovary, and endometrial thickness/pattern (optimal: periovulatory trilaminar "triple line" ≥7-8mm).

guias.titulo: Ovulation induction — Follicular size for the hCG trigger
guias.fuente: ASRM Practice Committee (2020), Fertil Steril 113(2):274-282 · ESHRE Female Infertility Guideline (2023), Hum Reprod Open 2023(3):hoad034
guias.html:
The hCG trigger mimics the endogenous LH surge: it resumes oocyte meiosis, luteinizes the granulosa cells, and times follicular rupture (36-40h after administration).

Trigger agents: Recombinant hCG (r-hCG) 250mcg SC · urinary hCG (u-hCG) 5,000-10,000 IU IM.

Follicular size by inducing agent:

  • Clomiphene citrate: trigger when the dominant follicle reaches a mean diameter of 18-20mm (tolerated up to 21-22mm — follicles under clomiphene tend to mature at slightly larger diameters).
  • Letrozole: trigger with the leading follicle at 18-20mm.
  • Gonadotropins (FSH/hMG): trigger with the leading follicle at 16-18mm (oocyte maturity is reached at slightly smaller sizes under direct gonadotropins; triggering above 19-20mm increases oocyte senescence).

Concurrent endometrial status: ideally ≥7mm with a trilaminar pattern before ordering the trigger.

Timing of intercourse/insemination: timed intercourse — the night of the trigger and again 36h later (or on alternating days: trigger day and the next). IUI — sperm preparation and insemination at 36h (range 34-38h) post-hCG.

guias.html:
In low-complexity techniques (timed intercourse/IUI), the safety threshold requires strictly avoiding high-order multiple pregnancy and Ovarian Hyperstimulation Syndrome (OHSS).

Immediate cancellation criteria — do NOT give hCG:

  • ≥3 mature follicles (≥15-16mm) in women <35 years, or >3-4 mature follicles in any low-complexity patient.
  • More than 4-6 intermediate follicles (11-14mm) that could respond to the trigger.
  • Serum estradiol >1,000-1,500pg/mL (if measured).

Management on cancellation: cancel and withhold the hCG trigger (it is the direct trigger for the VEGF cascade and capillary hyperpermeability of OHSS). Advise strict coital abstinence or mandatory condom use for ≥7-10 days. Do not give hCG for luteal support. Rescue option at a high-complexity center: convert the cycle to IVF with follicular aspiration, GnRH-agonist trigger, and total embryo cryopreservation ("freeze-all").

guias.titulo: Ovulation induction — Treatment failure and drug resistance
guias.html:
Drug resistance: persistent absence of recruitment, or no follicles ≥15mm despite maximum doses. Clomiphene resistance: anovulation after 150mg/day x5 days. Letrozole resistance: anovulation after 7.5mg/day x5 days. Management: switch therapeutic line (CC→Letrozole, add Metformin in PCOS with insulin resistance, or move to low-dose gonadotropins).

Failed induction (treatment failure): confirmed regular ovulatory cycles (optimal follicular development, follicular rupture and adequate luteal phase with progesterone ≥10ng/mL) without pregnancy after 4-6 consecutive ovulatory cycles. Management: full couple re-evaluation (tubal patency by HSG if not yet done, repeat semen analysis with TMSC) and escalation to high-complexity ART (IVF/ICSI).

Endometrial failure (antiestrogenic effect): adequate follicular growth but persistently thin endometrium (<6-7mm) in the preovulatory window (common with clomiphene). Management: switch to letrozole or add exogenous estrogen support.

guias.titulo: HPV vaccination — Paraguay PAI schedule and WHO/SAGE corroboration
guias.fuente: MSPyBS/PAI Paraguay. HPV vaccine — official material from the Expanded Program on Immunization · WHO SAGE. Human papillomavirus vaccines: WHO position paper, December 2022, Wkly Epidemiol Rec
guias.html:
Group 1 — Girls and boys aged 9 to 14 (routine schedule): 1 dose, administered at first contact.

Group 2 — Women aged 15 to 24 with no vaccination history (catch-up schedule): ages 15-20 → 1 dose at first contact. Ages 21-24 → 2 doses (at contact and at 6 months, minimum interval of 6 months).

Group 3 — People aged 15 to 45 with risk criteria (includes men and women except item 5):

  • HIV: 3 doses — at contact, at 1 month and at 6 months after the first dose.
  • Solid-organ or hematopoietic-component transplant recipients: 3 doses — same schedule (0-1-6 months).
  • Immunosuppressive treatment: 3 doses — at 6 months after the first dose, per the PAI schedule.
  • Survivors of sexual abuse: 2 doses — at contact and at 6 months after the first dose.
  • Women with cervical pathology (carriers of high-risk oncogenic HPV by HPV testing, or diagnosed with CIN 1/CIN 2 by Pap smear or biopsy): 3 doses (at contact, 1 month and 6 months) — preferably before conization/LEEP; if not possible, up to 1 year after excisional treatment.

The vaccine is free and available at health services (USF) under the Paraguay PAI schedule. Recording the dose in the vaccination card is recommended.

WHO/SAGE corroboration (December 2022): the SAGE position endorses 1-dose schedules for the general population aged 9-20 (non-inferior efficacy vs. 2 doses in compared immunogenicity trials), and maintains a 2-3 dose schedule for immunocompromised individuals (including HIV) — consistent with the 3-dose reinforcement that the Paraguayan schedule maintains for the Group 3 risk categories. There is no contradiction between the two sources; the PAI schedule is, if anything, more conservative (2 doses at ages 21-24) than the minimum SAGE allows.
